analysis: The uniform-transition weighting ablation succeeded on validation: macro HR@10 increased from the reported parent score of 0.505 to 0.520 (+0.015 absolute). Category HR@10 was 0.525 for Movies_and_TV, 0.560 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.430 for Electronics, and 0.565 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Parent category metrics were not supplied, so category-level improvements cannot be established. Equal weighting may preserve useful supervision from older transitions while per-history normalization prevents long histories from dominating; this mechanism remains a hypothesis supported by one fixed-seed comparison. No test results are available.
code_summary: Train one independent ConvRec model per category from seed 42, loading exactly one selected checkpoint per category at inference. The network uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations (1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8), two-head causal attention with jointly learned relative-distance bias, layer normalization, dropout, and jointly learned item scoring biases. Training uses cross-entropy over one positive and 512 sampled negatives per transition. The sole ablation removes exponential recency weights and assigns equal weight to valid transitions, averaging within each history and then across nonempty histories. AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, random-prefix augmentation, validation checkpoint selection, early stopping, four-category routing, and predictor interfaces remain unchanged. No ensembles, checkpoint averaging, or separately fitted scores are used.
